nodes.name: Role system
nodes.does: Gives every agent a named seat with defined powers: an executive office (a lead, a watchdog, an assistant, a researcher, an auditor) plus development pods, each with a builder, an independent reviewer, and a sealed final examiner. Seats are permanent; the AI occupying a seat is replaceable.
nodes.built: Shipped in v0.5.0. Role cards, fallback ladders, and the rule that no agent may review its own work are in the published protocol text.

nodes.name: Boot contracts and receipts
nodes.does: No agent works anonymously. Before doing anything, each agent must file a receipt stating who it is, what seat it holds, which folder and code version it’s on, and what it may touch. A missing or false receipt stops the agent.
nodes.built: Shipped; the referee validates receipts mechanically. The Aug-14 run showed receipt wording needs verbatim templates — that fix rides the next release.

nodes.name: Delegation and delivery proof
nodes.does: An assignment isn’t “sent” until it’s proven to have arrived: typed into the right terminal, actually submitted (Enter really pressed), and seen on screen. Kills the classic failure of instructions sitting unsent in an input box.
nodes.built: Shipped — and this one is YOUR bug: the June-13 send-vs-submit report became the delivery-verdict system and per-harness submit profiles.

nodes.name: Gates and bounded states
nodes.does: Checkpoints an agent cannot talk its way past: prove you read your instructions (file fingerprints), prove your location, pass readiness probes. Plus a fixed status vocabulary — BLOCKED or QA_PENDING exist; an unqualified “done” does not.
nodes.built: Shipped: activation gates, instruction-read proof, layout gate, ~20 deterministic validators. Field-tested Aug 14: caught all 7 incidents before corruption.

nodes.name: Closeout and audit trail
nodes.does: How a session ends honestly: final states, metrics, an evidence ledger, and a handoff the next session can resume from. Finished teams are parked, not vaporized.
nodes.built: Shipped. The Aug-14 session produced a complete worked example: a fingerprint-chained 31-ruling record and a verified closeout bundle.

nodes.name: Protocol bundle service
nodes.does: The heart of the referee: serves the versioned rulebook to any AI agent — startup packets sized to each role, role cards, receipt templates — so a fresh agent is governed in seconds, not after 100KB of pasted rules.
nodes.built: Shipped as npm @bradheitmann/odin-sentinel v0.5.0 (published = repo). ~48 tools and resources. This surface grew from your June-20 RFC sweep.

nodes.name: Deterministic validators
nodes.does: The referee’s whistle: mechanical checkers for receipts, delegations, delivery proofs, manifests, read-proofs. Deterministic = same input, same verdict — agents can’t argue.
nodes.built: Shipped; ~20 validators. 0.6.0 adds the truth-label check — built and reviewed, awaiting its sealed exam.

nodes.name: Surface layout and topology
nodes.does: Computes the canonical on-screen seating of a governed team and gates team growth behind a checklist. If work isn’t on a visible surface, it isn’t governed work.
nodes.built: Shipped. Used live Aug 14 to bootstrap a 16-seat organization from one pane.

nodes.name: Harness probes and pacing
nodes.does: Knows each agent CLI’s quirks (Claude Code, Codex, Droid, Pi, Crush…): installed, logged in, actually ready — and how fast you can type at it. “Installed” is not “provisioned.”
nodes.built: Shipped — your June-27 Pi rapid-fire report is why pacing exists. Aug-14 discoveries (Pi /clear trap, Droid double-Enter) queued for the matrix.

nodes.name: Telemetry and session reports
nodes.does: Collects what happened in a run — who did what, what was accepted, where tokens went — with secrets scrubbed before anything is stored or shared.
nodes.built: Shipped (session reports, redaction preview, telemetry config).

nodes.name: odin-watch liveness
nodes.does: A watcher that reads agent panes and classifies them: working, waiting, stuck, or dead — so nobody reads sixteen terminals by hand.
nodes.built: Shipped for cmux; tmux backend is a planned epic. The ownership rule wires in here during the circuit-breaker work.

nodes.name: Installs on this machine
nodes.does: Where governed sessions happen here: the Claude Code plugin, skill copies for other CLIs, and the cmux workspaces where teams get visible seats.
nodes.built: Working, two drift findings (Aug 19): plugin at 0.4.13 vs canon 0.5.0, and the master skill folder went missing in the Aug-8 recovery — installed copies have no source of truth to sync against.
nodes.cond: Restore the master skill dir, then update the plugin. The master matters more.

nodes.name: Downstream projects
nodes.does: Other repos running under this protocol: edge-agentic (planning law), llm-serve (local models), the migration-lab (whose failure report started the current build), and Deck — consuming odin-sentinel as a library for its cockpit.
nodes.built: Live consumers via npm 0.5.0. Two hand-offs are written and waiting for your paste: the edge-agentic assignment and the migration-lab reply.
nodes.cond: Two outbound notes drafted Aug 14, still undelivered.

nodes.name: Field feedback intake
nodes.does: Where your other projects’ pain becomes this project’s roadmap. Reports arrive, get fingerprint-verified, judged item by item, and accepted items become planned work. Nothing is silently dropped.
nodes.built:
All 7 reports accounted, none wasted:
• 06-13 Enter-key bug → shipped
• 06-20 RFC sweep → shipped (seeded 0.5.0)
• 06-27 Pi rapid-fire → shipped
• 06-28 provider outage → mostly shipped
• 07-08 stale-address → planned (EPIC-040)
• 07-08 roster/PO mandate → planned (EPIC-039–045)
• 08-08 governance displacement → in build
An independent audit confirmed this accounting; 3 sentence-sized omissions found and pinned.
nodes.good: Verdict: 3 shipped · 1 mostly · 1 in build · 2 planned · 0 lost.

nodes.name: Governance circuit breakers
nodes.does: The flagship build (EPIC-052), born from the Aug-8 failure report: a tamper-proof event logbook, a three-strikes retry limit that can’t be laundered, a ban on audits-of-audits without your sign-off, paperwork budgets that stop instead of spiral, and problems that don’t count as handled until someone owns them.
nodes.built: Wave-0 slice 1 BUILT and review-passed (570 tests green, fingerprint-protected). Slice 2 blocked after 3 attempts — every failure was procedure, never code — awaiting a machine-friendlier re-planned contract.
nodes.cond: Slice W0B needs its re-plan. Nothing ships without the full review chain and your commit approval.

nodes.name: Rulebook amendments
nodes.does: Seven precise rulebook edits (EPIC-053) closing the loopholes the failure report exposed, plus one code change: every serious claim carries a truth label (observed / derived / claimed…) so “claimed” can never again pass as “done.”
nodes.built: Amendments BUILT, review-passed 16/16. Final gate — the sealed exam — parked on your decision after five examiner seats fell to procedure. Becomes v0.6.0.
nodes.cond: Sealed exam awaits your go; then commit approval; then 0.6.0.

traceText.RO-BC: Seats are defined; every occupant must file a receipt to claim one.
traceText.BC-DL: A seated agent may receive work — but only through proven delivery.
traceText.DL-GA: Delivered work can’t start until the gates pass: read-proof, location-proof, readiness.
traceText.GA-CL: Work that passes its gates flows to honest closeout: evidence, metrics, handoff.
traceText.RO-PB: The rulebook is compiled into the bundle the referee serves to agents.
traceText.PB-VD: Every receipt and proof an agent files hits a deterministic validator.
traceText.PB-CC: The referee installs locally: a plugin for Claude Code, skills for the other CLIs.
traceText.CC-DS: Governed sessions run in downstream projects, consuming the published package.
traceText.DS-FB: When something breaks in the field, it comes back as a written report.
traceText.FB-CB: The Aug-8 failure report was judged, accepted, and became the circuit-breaker build.
traceText.FB-DA: The same report’s process lessons became seven rulebook amendments.
traceText.DA-RO: Amendments, once past their sealed exam and your approval, change the rulebook.
traceText.CB-PB: The breakers ship into the referee as v0.6.0 — and the loop continues.

title: ODIN SENTINEL — Governance Protocol · Architecture Map

intro.title: A rulebook your agent teams cannot quietly break
intro.sub: what this project is, what state it’s in, and what happened to your feedback
intro.proseHTML:
What this is

When you run several AI coding agents at once, three things go wrong: they do hidden work you can’t see, they claim things are done that aren’t, and they quietly step on each other’s files. ODIN Sentinel is the fix: a written rulebook (the SCP protocol) plus a small local referee program (an MCP server) that any AI agent can load. No cloud service, no AI of its own — just rules and a referee.

Fly the map the standard way: drag to orbit (one finger on a phone or iPad), scroll or pinch to zoom, right-drag or two-finger drag to pan. The city is a loop — rulebook district (north), the referee (center), where it runs (east), and the feedback loop (south) that turns field failures into the next improvement.

Was your feedback wasted? No.

Seven field reports: 3 fully shipped, 1 mostly shipped, 1 in build now, 2 planned. Click FB for the report-by-report accounting.

Reading the roofs

Color is attention debt: paper is healthy, amber owes work, blue is being built, red is broken. A number painted on a roof counts its open items (red glyph = a blocker is among them); a slate diamond on a roof means a decision of yours is inside. Click any marked block: the camera flies to it and the panel lists its items.
